For the Informant : Mr. A.K. Chaturvedy, Advocate
-----
03/11.11.2024

The petitioner is apprehending his arrest for the offences punishable under Sections
376/506 of the Indian Penal Code in connection with Sadar (Chatra) P.S. Case No. 249/2024,
pending in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chatra.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case and has not committed any offence as alleged in the F.I.R.
The story made out in the written report is completely false and concocted.
The petitioner neither committed rape upon the informant nor blackmailed her as has been alleged.
Though the alleged occurrence took place on 29.06.2024, however, the F.I.R was lodged on 16.07.2024 without assigning any valid reason for such delay.
Hence, he may be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.
3. Learned A.P.P as well as learned counsel for the informant oppose the petitioner's prayer for anticipatory bail.

Learned A.P.P submits that the statement of the informant/victim has also been recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C in which she has fully supported the case of the prosecution and hence, the petitioner does not deserve the privilege of anticipatory bail.
4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the nature of allegation made against the petitioner, I am not inclined to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.
5. Accordingly, the prayer for anticipatory bail of the abovenamed petitioner is rejected.
